title: The Deadline of the DMZ
premise: Sebastian Almeida, a veteran interpreter for a doomed peace delegation at the Korean DMZ, receives calls on a burner phone from a voice they buried years ago — their former handler, presumed dead, who reveals that the 'training program' that made Sebastian an asset never ended; it simply changed owners. As the delegation collapses on schedule, Sebastian discovers the talks are cover for a handover of the network to a buyer who intends to weaponize interpreters embedded in governments worldwide. With a ragged found family — a defector archivist, a disgraced negotiator, and the handler who may be savior or bait — Sebastian must burn the network's ledger before the transfer closes at midnight on the armistice anniversary. They succeed, but only by surrendering the one thing the network gave them: the ability to disappear.
about_author: Coral Eastwick is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working multilateral summits before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose professional gift — fluency — becomes their deepest liability.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: Sebastian Almeida's POV. Opening day of the Panmunjom peace talks; Sebastian interprets a concession they know is scripted to fail. Establishes their precision, exhaustion, and twelve years of obeying rewritten rules. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A burner phone appears in their hotel Bible, ringing with the voice of Mara Voss — the handler who died in 2019. She says three words: 'The ledger lives.' Beat: vertigo; the past refusing burial.

chapters.title: Delegation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Negotiator Ingrid Halvorsen's POV. Ingrid suspects her own delegation is sabotaging the talks and quietly recruits Sebastian as her ears. Beat: two wary professionals recognizing each other's loneliness.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rewrites
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Sebastian's POV. The training program: how a lonely linguistics student was groomed into an asset whose translations could start or stop wars. Beat: grief for the person they were before.

chapters.title: Second Call
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Mara gives coordinates inside the DMZ joint security area and a deadline: the armistice anniversary, eleven days out. Sebastian goes, finds a dead drop, and a photo of themselves they never posed for. Beat: hunted feeling.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Defector archivist Yoon Ji-ho's POV. Ji-ho has spent six years copying the network's recruitment files and recognizes Sebastian's name in them. He approaches not to blackmail but because he needs a translator. Beat: tentative alliance.

chapters.title: Scripted Failure
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. The talks collapse exactly on schedule; Ingrid realizes the failure was the product being sold. She confronts Sebastian with what she knows. Beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Ji-ho's POV. The ledger: forty-one embedded interpreters across nine governments, all trained by the same program, now being transferred to a private buyer codenamed CORMORANT. Beat: scale of horror dawning.

chapters.title: Mara, Alive
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Face-to-face with Mara in a Seoul bathhouse. She claims she faked her death to infiltrate the sale — but she also trained Sebastian, and lies were her first language. Beat: longing and suspicion entwined.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The found family convenes in Ji-ho's basement archive: rules, roles, mutual distrust. Ingrid brings diplomatic access, Ji-ho the files, Mara the tradecraft. Beat: fragile belonging forming.

chapters.title: Interpreter Zero
chapters.summary: Flashback, Mara's POV. How she recruited Sebastian twelve years ago and what it cost her conscience. Reveals she has been protecting Sebastian longer than they knew. Beat: guilt made human.

chapters.title: First Burn
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Ji-ho's POV, alternating. They test-expose one embedded asset through a controlled leak; the asset vanishes within hours — erased, not arrested. Beat: the network's terrifying efficiency demonstrated.

chapters.title: CORMORANT Surfaces
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. At a reception, Ingrid identifies the buyer's broker: Anton Reiss, a 'cultural attaché' whose accent Sebastian places instantly as fabricated. Beat: the enemy gains a face.

chapters.title: Tail Numbers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian realizes they're being followed by someone using their own tradecraft — their own tells. Paranoia fractures the team's trust in Mara. Beat: isolation inside the family.

chapters.title: The Forty-First Name
chapters.summary: Ji-ho's POV. The ledger lists forty assets — plus a forty-first entry, redacted except for a recruitment date matching Sebastian's. Beat: dread; Sebastian may be inventory, not hunter.

chapters.title: Safehouse Sonata
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. A rare quiet night: cooking, languages traded like gifts, Ingrid teaching card games, Ji-ho playing piano. Beat: found family crystallizing — raising the stakes for its loss.

chapters.title: Reiss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Reiss corners Sebastian privately: join the new ownership, keep your skills, keep your life. He knows everything, including the safehouse. Beat: temptation wearing a polite smile.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Someone fed Reiss the safehouse address. Suspicion falls on Mara, whose death was too convenient. Ingrid demands answers; Mara offers none. Beat: trust cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian interrogates Mara using the program's own methods against her — and hates how easily they come back. She admits half-truths: she didn't fake her death alone. Beat: intimacy weaponized, then regretted.

chapters.title: Halfway Line
chapters.summary: Ji-ho's POV. Midpoint revelation: the transfer isn't a sale — it's a merger. CORMORANT is the program's original architect, returning to reclaim his creation, and the anniversary deadline is his homecoming. Beat: the true shape of the enemy.

chapters.title: The Panmunjom Gambit
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Plan formed: use the failed talks' closing ceremony as cover to access the delegation's secure comms room where the transfer will be authenticated. Beat: purpose replacing fear.

chapters.title: Practice Runs
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Rehearsals for the infiltration; Sebastian must interpret live while running the op, their two selves finally merged. Beat: competence reclaimed as identity.

chapters.title: Compromised Frequency
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The team discovers their planning channel has been monitored since Chapter 10 — meaning the enemy has heard every plan. Beat: despair; the trap was built around them.

chapters.title: Split the Family
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. To survive, they split: false plan broadcast on the compromised channel, real plan kept oral and unrecorded. Each member gets a piece no one else holds. Beat: trust as operational necessity.

chapters.title: Ji-ho's Price
chapters.summary: Ji-ho's POV. Ji-ho reveals why he really defected: his sister is entry nineteen in the ledger, still embedded in Pyongyang's delegation. He wants extraction, not just exposure. Beat: personal cost made explicit.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The city prepares to mark the armistice; fireworks tests rattle windows. Sebastian visits the site of their recruitment and burns their old training manual. Beat: mourning the self the program built.

chapters.title: Ceremony
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Closing ceremony begins; dignitaries speak peace over a machine of war. Sebastian interprets flawlessly while the clock runs toward midnight authentication. Beat: terrible poise.

chapters.title: Comms Room
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Mara's POV. Infiltration succeeds — until the comms room lights up with Reiss waiting, applauding. The false plan worked on everyone except him. Beat: cold shock.

chapters.title: The Architect Speaks
chapters.summary: Reiss/CORMORANT's monologue, framed through Sebastian's POV. He doesn't want to kill them; he wants Sebastian to authenticate the transfer — the fortieth asset signing over the other thirty-nine. Beat: horror of complicity offered as destiny.

chapters.title: Refusal in Two Languages
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian refuses — in the program's coded dialect, telling every hidden listener the truth aloud. Assets worldwide begin receiving the warning. Beat: defiance as translation.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara takes the bullet meant for Sebastian, buying seconds, and dies — this time truly — whispering that the ledger copy was always in Sebastian's hands. Beat: sacrifice and revelation.

chapters.title: Midnight Authentication
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax: Sebastian reaches the terminal as the countdown closes and uploads Ji-ho's corrupted ledger — poisoning the transfer with falsified entries that flag every asset to their own governments. Beat: white-knuckle triumph.

chapters.title: Firewall
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Ingrid holds the corridor, trading her career and nearly her life to buy Sebastian ninety seconds. Beat: courage without glory.

chapters.title: Extraction Nineteen
chapters.summary: Ji-ho's POV. Simultaneously, Ji-ho uses the chaos to pull his sister out via a pre-arranged defection route. It works, barely. Beat: grief and grace in the same breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath, First Light
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Dawn over the DMZ. The transfer failed; Reiss vanished; thirty-nine interpreters wake to messages that free or damn them. Sebastian waits to be arrested. Beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Closed-door hearings. Ingrid spends every favor she has left to frame Sebastian as a whistleblower, not an asset. Beat: loyalty repaid at ruinous cost.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian surrenders their anonymity — testifying publicly, ending any chance of disappearing again. The network's last power over them dissolves because they have nothing left to hide. Beat: liberation through exposure.

chapters.title: The Basement Archive Opens
chapters.summary: Ji-ho's POV. The archive becomes a protection service for extracted interpreters — a counter-network built on consent instead of coercion. Beat: the theme answered; family institutionalized.

chapters.title: A Familiar Ringtone
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Months later, a burner phone rings. Sebastian answers. On the line: a frightened voice speaking the program's dialect — another asset, reaching out. Beat: the story's cycle turned toward rescue.

chapters.title: The Deadline That Passed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, closing. At the next anniversary, Sebastian stands at Panmunjom not as property but as witness, interpreting openly for the families of the disappeared. Final beat: belonging chosen, not assigned — and the work continuing.
